text: Which the receiver therefore combine in different ways. For example, if the signals that arrive at the receiver arrive more or less with the same delay, so with the same phase, they will all be more or less in phase, like in this figure. So we have the so-called constructive interference, meaning that they are multiple copies of the same signal that overlap at the receiver, and they are all more or less aligned with respect to each other. So the receiver will just get the sum of these signals. But instead, if these signals that arrive at the receiver have different delays, so different phases, and by chance they are in opposite phase, then they nullify each other, and the receiver essentially gets nothing, because because they have opposite phases.
